scalesUsed.application: The primary scale for all of B.B. King's lead work, providing the melodic vocabulary for his signature licks and phrases

scalesUsed.notes: B - D - E - F - F# - A
scalesUsed.application: Adds the blue note (F natural) for gritty bends and chromatic passing tones in lead phrases

scalesUsed.notes: B - C# - D - E - F# - G - A
scalesUsed.application: Provides additional note choices (C# and G) for melodic variation and connection between pentatonic positions

keyAndScale.relativeMinor: B minor is the relative minor of D major

mainProgression.description: A minor blues progression using the classic i-iv-V7 structure, creating a sophisticated and melancholic harmonic backdrop for B.B. King's vocal and guitar phrasing

sectionProgressions.progression: Bm - Bm - Bm - Bm | Em - Em - Bm - Bm | F#7 - Em - Bm - F#7
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: i - i - i - i | iv - iv - i - i | V7 - iv - i - V7
sectionProgressions.description: Standard 12-bar blues adapted to minor key, with the V7 (F#7) providing dominant tension and resolution
Simple turnaround using the dominant V7 chord to cycle back to the top of the progression

sectionProgressions.progression: Bm - Bm - Em - Em - Bm - F#7
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: i - i - iv - iv - i - V7
sectionProgressions.description: Same 12-bar structure provides the harmonic foundation for B.B. King's celebrated guitar solos

harmonicFunction: Bm (i) - Tonic minor center establishing the melancholic, introspective mood
Em (iv) - Subdominant minor movement adding emotional depth and harmonic motion
F#7 (V7) - Dominant seventh creating strong tension and pull back to the tonic
The minor blues structure gives the song its sophisticated, sorrowful character

techniques.name: B.B. King Vibrato
techniques.description: B.B. King's signature rapid finger vibrato technique, where the entire hand rocks quickly to produce a fast, shimmering vibrato that gives each note an intensely vocal quality

notes: B.B. King's vibrato is faster and tighter than most rock vibrato
Generated by rapidly rocking the fretting finger back and forth
The wrist stays relatively still - motion comes from finger rocking
Applied to nearly every sustained note in his playing
Creates a vocal, singing quality that is B.B. King's trademark
Often combined with string bending for maximum expression
sequence: Fret a note firmly with the index or ring finger
Keep the thumb anchored behind the neck for leverage
Rapidly rock the fretting finger side to side (not up and down)
Maintain even speed and width of the vibrato
Apply immediately upon picking the note for maximum effect
tips: Practice on the B string at the 7th-10th frets first
Start slow and build speed gradually
B.B. King uses the 'butterfly' vibrato (finger rocking, not wrist bending)
Listen carefully to recordings to match the speed and width
The vibrato should be even and controlled, never random
details.progression: Applied throughout all B minor pentatonic phrases

techniques.name: Expressive String Bending
techniques.description: Precise, soulful string bending that is the cornerstone of B.B. King's lead style, using half-step, whole-step, and quarter-tone bends to imitate the human voice

notes: Whole-step bends on the B string (7th to 9th fret area) are signature
Half-step bends for blue note inflections and subtle expression
Quarter-tone bends (microtonal) for vocal-like crying effect
Pre-bends: bend the string before picking, then release
Bends often resolve to chord tones of the underlying harmony
B.B. King rarely played more than a few notes at a time
sequence: Support the bending finger with adjacent fingers behind it
Push the string upward (toward the ceiling) on the higher strings
Bend to exact pitch - use a tuner to verify
Hold the bend at the top and add vibrato
Release slowly for a controlled descent
tips: Always use multiple fingers to support bends
Practice bending to exact pitch against a reference note
B.B. King's bends are vocal and deliberate, never rushed
Try bending into target notes of each chord in the progression
Less is more - a single perfect bend is worth more than many sloppy ones

techniques.name: Call-and-Response Phrasing
techniques.description: The conversation between vocal lines and guitar responses that defines B.B. King's style - the guitar answers, echoes, and comments on the vocal melody

notes: Guitar phrases respond to vocal lines in the spaces between lyrics
Each guitar phrase is short (2-5 notes) but highly expressive
Phrases typically start after the vocal line ends
Uses B minor pentatonic in the upper register (B string, 7th-12th fret)
Each response should feel like a musical answer to a question
B.B. King never played while singing - creating natural spaces
sequence: Listen to the vocal phrase and identify the space that follows
Play a short, melodic response in the gap
End the guitar phrase before the next vocal line begins
Vary the response: sometimes mirror the vocal, sometimes contrast it
tips: Practice with the original recording to learn the timing of each response
Keep guitar phrases short and meaningful
Think of the guitar as having a conversation with the vocals
Each response should feel complete - don't leave phrases hanging
Study B.B. King's economy of notes - say more with less
details.progression: Responses played over the 12-bar Bm - Em - F#7 structure

sections.name: Intro
sections.description: The atmospheric opening with orchestral strings setting the mood, followed by B.B. King's first guitar statement - a few perfectly placed bent notes that establish the song's emotional tone
notes: Orchestral strings establish the minor key atmosphere
B.B. King enters with a few deliberate, bent notes
Each note has signature vibrato applied immediately
Clean tone with slight warmth from the hollow-body guitar

sections.name: Verse (12-Bar Blues)
sections.description: The verse follows a 12-bar minor blues structure with B.B. King's vocals answered by short, expressive guitar phrases in the gaps between lyric lines
sections.progression: Bm - Bm - Bm - Bm | Em - Em - Bm - Bm | F#7 - Em - Bm - F#7
notes: Guitar responds to vocal lines in the spaces between lyrics
Each guitar phrase is short but packed with expression
Bending and vibrato are applied to almost every note
The guitar complements rather than competes with the vocals

sections.name: Guitar Solo
sections.description: B.B. King's masterful guitar solo showcasing his signature vibrato, precise bending, and minimalist phrasing - proving that a handful of perfectly executed notes can be more powerful than hundreds of fast ones
sections.progression: Bm - Bm - Em - Em - Bm - F#7
notes: Based in B minor pentatonic around the 7th-12th fret area
Every note features B.B. King's trademark vibrato
Bends are deliberate and land on exact target pitches
Phrasing is spacious with generous pauses between ideas

sections.name: Outro Solo
sections.description: The extended outro solo where B.B. King stretches out with increasingly emotional phrases, building intensity through repetition and slight variation of key melodic motifs
notes: Extended improvisation over the repeating 12-bar form
Builds emotional intensity through repetition and variation
Moves between the 7th and 12th fret positions
The fade-out features some of B.B. King's most passionate playing

alternatives: Any semi-hollow or hollow-body guitar with humbuckers
guitar.pickup: Neck humbucker for warm, round blues tone

settings.treble: 6 (bright enough to cut but not harsh)

effects.reverb: Built-in amp spring reverb, light to moderate amount
effects.other: No effects pedals - B.B. King's tone comes entirely from his fingers, guitar, and amp

beginner.focus: Learn the basic chord shapes and understand the 12-bar minor blues structure
steps: Master Bm, Em, and F#7 chord shapes
Learn the 12-bar minor blues form and practice counting bars
Practice B minor pentatonic scale in the open and 7th fret positions
Work on basic string bending technique on the B string

intermediate.focus: Develop B.B. King vibrato technique and expressive phrasing
steps: Practice B.B. King-style finger vibrato at various speeds
Learn to bend strings to exact pitch (half-step and whole-step)
Study the call-and-response phrasing between voice and guitar
Learn the main solo phrases note by note

advanced.focus: Master the full song with authentic phrasing, dynamics, and improvisational ability
steps: Perform the complete song with all solos and fills
Develop the ability to improvise over the 12-bar form
Achieve authentic B.B. King vibrato and bending tone
Work on creating your own call-and-response phrases
advanced.timeEstimate: 6-10 weeks for complete mastery and improvisation

commonMistakes: Playing too many notes - B.B. King's power is in restraint and space
Vibrato that is uneven or too slow - practice for consistency
Bending out of tune - always verify bends against reference pitches
Not leaving space between phrases - silence is part of the music
Using too much gain or distortion - B.B. King played clean
practiceRoutine: Warm up with B minor pentatonic scale in multiple positions (5 minutes)
Vibrato exercises: sustain single notes with controlled vibrato (10 minutes)
Bending practice: bend to exact pitches on the B and G strings (10 minutes)
Practice call-and-response: play along with the recording, filling gaps (10 minutes)
Improvise over a 12-bar Bm backing track focusing on phrasing (10 minutes)
focusAreas: B.B. King-style rapid finger vibrato technique
Accurate string bending to target pitches
Call-and-response timing between vocals and guitar
metronomeWork: Practice the 12-bar form counting bars at 88 BPM
Slow vibrato exercises at 60 BPM, building to match B.B. King's speed
Bending exercises: one bend per beat at 70 BPM, focus on accuracy
Full song play-through at 88 BPM with focus on phrasing and groove
